_comment: guarantees.json — machine-readable form of the GUARANTEES.md claims table (issue #710). The doc's table is RENDERED from this file; tools/check_guarantees.py fails the build when a rule id here no longer exists in the diagnostics registry, when a corpus fixture's registered verdict contradicts the row it pins, when a scoped rule id appears in no row (and is not declared in `unclaimed` with a reason), or when a row carries no evidence. Edit this file, then run `python3 tools/check_guarantees.py --render`.

scope.note: The claims table is about Tier-0 (ownership & sendability, HYB-E3xx) plus the managed-block lint (HYB-E8xx). Codes in these families must be claimed by a row or listed in `unclaimed` with a reason — a new rule that silently lands in no row fails the guard.

rows.does: Every argument classified by the six sendable classes; shared mutable aliases rejected
rows.claim: **Guaranteed**: no value reaches a spawned task through an unproven path

rows.does: Same classification as spawn; failures `HYB-E3002` with a fix-it menu
rows.claim: **Guaranteed**: the sent value is moved, frozen, copied, or knowingly managed

rows.does: **Deep** sendability: every reference-typed field/element must itself be sendable; a fresh literal wrapping a shared map is still rejected
rows.claim: **Guaranteed**: embedding an alias does not launder it

rows.does: **Fail-closed**: unproven values are rejected (`HYB-E3005`) — never silently passed as safe. Fix-its: ascribe / route through a channel / take the hatch
rows.claim: **Guaranteed**: the checker never blesses what it cannot resolve
rows.evidence_md: §9.3 O4.9 (rule FC); dedicated checker tests; corpus `34-select-send-unproven-name`

rows.does: `task`/send statements inside a closure are real boundaries (goroutines in the emitted Go) and are checked fail-closed, `managed`-escapable
rows.claim: **Guaranteed** for boundary statements; a closure that writes a captured mutable binding and is passed to a foreign Go call is checked too (HYB-E3013, the [A5](SPEC-LANGUAGE.md) fourth check-site); captures without a boundary statement or an escape write remain **outside**
rows.evidence_md: §9.3 O4.10; corpus [10](tests/checker-corpus/10-a5-http-handler-capture.hy) flipped ACCEPT→REJECT by the A5 fourth check-site (W-016 M2/M3) per its own pre-registered OQ1 condition

rows.does: Ownership transfer with use-after-move rejected (`HYB-E3003`)
rows.claim: **Guaranteed**: a moved value cannot be used by the sender afterwards

rows.does: Polonius-style dataflow over borrows/loans; conflict-free proven or rejected
rows.claim: **Guaranteed** within the checked subset
rows.evidence_md: §9.1 rules O1–O3 (E31xx family); checker unit tests

rows.does: Explicit hatch: linted (`HYB-E8001`), payload REQUIRED (bare block rejects `HYB-E0003`; unknown category rejects `HYB-E0004` — closed set: mutex/atomic/actor/finalizer/interop/other), greppable, counted per category (`--report-managed`), optionally forbidden (`--deny-managed`), and CI-gated for NEW blocks (`tools/managed_gate.py` + baseline)
rows.claim: **No soundness claim inside** — it is a compile-time permit, not a synchronization mechanism. The escape is auditable, never silent

rows.surface: Values escaping into Go APIs (net/http handlers, callbacks)
rows.does: A closure that writes a captured mutable binding and is passed to a foreign (package-qualified) Go call is a fourth check-site: rejects with HYB-E3013 unless the call site takes `managed("...", "interop")` or the capture is const/non-`may_share`; read-only captures stay outside the checker
rows.claim: **Guaranteed** (HYB-E3013) for captured-write escapes; read-only captures are **outside** — Go's DRF-SC with `-race` as the backstop
rows.evidence_md: §8.5 (A5 promoted to a fourth check-site, W-016 M2/M3); §9.2; corpus [10](tests/checker-corpus/10-a5-http-handler-capture.hy) pins the reject

rows.does: Not in the curated surface today; a value of a foreign/unmodeled type at a check-site is **unproven → rejected** (fail-closed), never silently allowed
rows.claim: **No claim**; fail-closed rejection instead of a false one

rows.does: **[TBD]** joins the curated surface post-MVP; when it lands, atomic-typed values become sendable-by-type (class 2). Until then: unproven → rejected
rows.claim: **No claim yet**; the growth path is pre-designed, not improvised

rows.does: Not modeled; the value itself is classified like any other at a check-site
rows.claim: **No claim** about cancellation semantics — the claim is about value sharing, not protocol liveness

rows.does: Not in the surface; not modeled
rows.claim: **No claim**

rows.does: **Reserved, not implemented** ([O20](SPEC-LANGUAGE.md)). There is **no memory-unsafe escape at all** in safe mode: raw cross-language pointers are forbidden, period
rows.claim: **No claim** because there is no surface to claim about

rows.does: Not part of `.hy`; cgo code in the surrounding Go project is foreign code the checker cannot see
rows.claim: **No claim**

rows.does: The checker proves value sendability, not send/close protocol ordering
rows.claim: **No claim** — a liveness/protocol property, out of Tier-0's scope

rows.does: Go's GC, unchanged — Hybrid emits Go source
rows.claim: **Inherited from Go**

rows.does: Single ownership, moves, function-local borrows; `panic = abort` at the boundary (never unwind across)
rows.claim: **Guaranteed by construction**

rows.does: Owning-side handle tables with generation tags; copy-small/pin-large borrows
rows.claim: **Guaranteed** by the Spike-3 design + tests

rows.does: Guard-checked fast path on the caller's stack; pooled guarded deep stacks; blocking callees via the two-tier scheduler with hard thread budgets
rows.claim: **Performance claimed and measured** (3.37–3.44 ns sandbox fast path; worker-tier 6.93 ns recorded honestly as a MISS vs the 5 ns budget)

unclaimed.HYB-E3004: the rule is enforced (a move applies to whole bindings and own-handle fields, not GC fields) but no corpus fixture pins it with EXPECTED-DIAGNOSTIC and no row claims it — claiming it needs a fixture first
unclaimed.HYB-E3006: const-binding immutability (T22) is enforced and pinned by corpus 27-const-write-reject / 38-const-closure-alias-write-reject, but the claims table carries no row for it — candidate row for the next doc revision
unclaimed.HYB-E3007: channel-usage rule (the target of a send must be a channel): enforced by the BUILDABLE sweep; row 2 claims sendability of the value, not channel typing
unclaimed.HYB-E3008: channel-direction rule (recv-only / send-only misuse): channel typing, outside the sendability claim of row 2
unclaimed.HYB-E3009: channel-direction rule (close / range): channel typing, outside the sendability claim of row 2
unclaimed.HYB-E3010: `break loop` / `continue loop` label rule: lexical, unrelated to Tier-0 ownership
unclaimed.HYB-E3011: channel element-type rule: typing, not sendability
unclaimed.HYB-E3012: channel direction conversion rule: typing, not sendability
